title: Functional role of skull lymphoid structures in CNS immunosurveillance.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Fetched GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) records and file lists for GSE309632 (4 samples: skull and brain-tumour single-cell RNA plus BCR, i.e. B-cell receptor, tables; RAW.tar 470 MB), GSE309634 (4 samples: skull and sternum B cells; 142 MB) and GSE313969 (3 samples: dura, skull, sternum T cells; 148 MB). Downloaded and parsed the two GSE309634 BCR contig tables: skull 6,348 contigs / 3,614 cells / 3,019 clonotypes; sternum 6,547 contigs / 3,927 cells / 3,036 clonotypes; 31 standard 10x Genomics columns (V/D/J/C gene, CDR3 amino-acid and nucleotide sequences, reads, UMIs).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That each sample is one sorted pool from mice (no per-mouse replicate in GEO metadata); that other data are 'available on request'; source data with the paper (not retrieved; Europe PMC supplement endpoint timed out). Did not open the 10x count-matrix tarballs (65-255 MB each).

a1_downloadable.note: GEO files download openly; checked file lists and opened BCR CSVs. Imaging and other data are 'available on request' only.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No measured outcome column. The only candidate label is tissue of origin (skull vs sternum vs dura vs brain), which is the sample identity itself; isotype (c_gene) is a column but is a generic, already-solved antibody task unrelated to this paper's biology.

a3_inputs_present.note: CDR3 and framework sequences are present in the BCR CSVs; gene-by-cell count matrices are in the tarballs (not opened).

a4_units_stated.note: Standard 10x Cell Ranger outputs (UMI counts, reads); units implicit but standard.

a5_enough_rows.note: 11 GEO samples across 3 series, one pooled sample per tissue per experiment. ~3,600-3,900 B cells per tissue, but the unit of replication for a tissue label is the sample, so effectively n=1 per class.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~0.8 GB compressed across all three series

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not cross-checked against paper cell counts; GEO sample counts are internally consistent.

a8_label_provenance.note: Tissue label equals the 10x lane/batch, so any cell-level classifier learns batch (sort, capture, sequencing run) as much as biology; leakage by construction.

backbone.name: scGPT or Geneformer (single-cell models); AntiBERTy or ESM-2 for BCR sequences

honest_claim_h3: A classifier could only claim to separate one pooled skull sample from one pooled sternum sample, not skull from sternum biology, because tissue and batch are the same thing.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use single-cell gene expression and antibody receptor sequences to predict whether a B cell came from skull or sternum bone marrow.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-cell gene counts and B-cell receptor sequences from GEO; 3,614 skull and 3,927 sternum B cells (verified in BCR tables), one pooled sample per tissue.
plain_idea.predict: The tissue a cell was sorted from, which is just the sample label assigned at sorting, not a separate measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Would show whether skull-marrow B cells carry a distinct signature, but with one sample per tissue the answer can't be separated from batch effects.

ml_idea: Tissue-of-origin classification of B/T cells (skull vs sternum vs dura) from expression and BCR/TCR sequence; not viable because each tissue is a single pooled sample.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from GEO file sizes; nothing timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count biological replicates per tissue in GEO: one sample per tissue per series, already done.

verdict_reason: Mouse mechanistic study with 11 pooled single-cell samples (one per tissue); no measured outcome column (A2), tissue label is confounded with batch (A8), and effectively n=1 per class (A5). Existing-model search skipped because Part A failed.
